scope: Author review of cited clauses and corresponding orientation boundaries; not jurisdiction-specific employer compliance certification.

rows.finding: 1904.35 requires reasonable prompt reporting procedures, employee information and non-retaliation; reporting need not wait for recordability classification.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: OSH Act section 5 separates employer duties from employee compliance. Section 11(c) protects exercise of statutory rights; the worker guidance states the 30-day retaliation complaint window. ESC01 distinguishes site stop-work arrangements from conditional statutory refusal rights.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.21(b)(2)-(5) requires instruction for actual work hazards, harmful substances, relevant plants/animals and flammable/toxic materials. General orientation does not replace site-specific instruction.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.20(b) assigns prevention programs and frequent inspections to the employer with designated competent persons; only employees qualified by training or experience may operate equipment.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.119(g) addresses covered-process operating instruction, understanding records and refresher intervals. The awareness credential is not a covered-process operator qualification.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.147(c)(7) distinguishes authorized, affected and other employees, tag limitations, change-triggered retraining and training records. ESC03 expressly preserves the drilling/servicing and construction exclusions in (a)(1)(ii); orientation does not authorize isolation.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.417 requires tagging deactivated controls and rendering deenergized equipment/circuits inoperative with tags identifying the affected equipment. Core recognition is not authority to perform circuit work.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.332 distinguishes job-related instruction for unqualified workers from qualified-person live-part identification, voltage and clearance skills. Core credential does not grant that qualified status.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.333(a)-(b) requires hazard-matched practices, deenergizing subject to specified exceptions, and treating uncontrolled deenergized parts as energized. ESC03 correctly rejects pushbutton OFF and visual locks as independent verification.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.335 requires task-appropriate electrical protection, inspection and safeguards; barriers, signs and sometimes attendants control access. It supplies no single universal arc rating.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.146(g) requires proficiency before assigned duties and when duties/hazards change; (k) requires evaluated rescue capability and role-specific preparation. ESC04 recognition and withdrawal do not grant entry or rescue authority.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.1207 requires understandable role training, proficiency and employer records; recognition instruction does not authorize entry or rescue.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.252(a) requires removal or protection of fire hazards and prohibits work when those controls cannot be provided. ESC04 hot-work recognition and authorization boundaries preserve these controls rather than treating a permit as protection.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.350-.354 separately address cylinder handling, electrical welding equipment, fire prevention, ventilation and coatings. Controls depend on materials and location; ESC04 does not authorize welding or coating removal based on this orientation.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.30(a)-(c) distinguishes qualified-person fall training and equipment instruction; retraining follows relevant change or inadequate skill.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.28(a) specifies fall-protection duties and exclusions; 1910.29 sets system criteria before exposure. ESC04 correctly avoids treating common height thresholds as universal and leaves personal-system selection and rescue to qualified task planning.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.503 requires competent-person construction fall instruction and a written certification record; course awareness is not the employer task certification.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.454 separates scaffold-user subject-qualified instruction from competent-person erection/moving/inspection training and requires retraining for changed hazards or inadequate proficiency.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.651(k) requires competent-person inspections and removal from hazardous excavation conditions; 1926.652(a) requires protective systems with specific exceptions. ESC04 does not allow learners to self-declare a shallow trench safe.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.179(b)(8) restricts crane operation to designated personnel; 1910.184(c)-(d) requires load separation, rated identified slings and competent-person inspection. ESC04 teaches exclusion-zone recognition without claiming rigging or crane competence.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.1427(a) distinguishes required training, certification/licensing and employer evaluation, including supervised trainees and specified equipment exceptions. Core explicitly grants no operator qualification.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.1428(c)(5) requires knowledge and practical tests for signalpersons; 1926.1430 requires applicable powerline, operator and signaling training. ESC04 uses agreed emergency stop communication without claiming signalperson qualification.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.1200(h) requires actual workplace chemical information, detection/protection and usable labels/SDS/program access. General chemical instruction must be supplemented for the workplace.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.59 incorporates the construction requirements identical to 1910.1200. ESC05 chemical instruction remains general and requires actual workplace labels, SDS and employer controls.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.134(f) requires individual fit testing for tight-fitting facepieces and additional testing for fit-affecting changes; (k) includes annual and change-triggered retraining.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.1000 distinguishes time-weighted, ceiling and peak limits rather than one universal safe concentration. ESC05-06 require identified exposure assessment and controls; smell or a single reading is not treated as clearance.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.1053(j)(3) requires demonstrated understanding of health effects, actual tasks, employer controls, the rule and medical surveillance. ESC06 teaches recognition and prevention but retains workplace-specific completion requirements.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.1153(i)(2) additionally identifies the employer-designated competent person and actual task controls. ESC06 does not substitute awareness credit for the construction employer program.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.1001(j)(7) prescribes understandable initial and annual training for covered exposures with workplace operations, controls and surveillance. ESC06 directs suspect material to evaluation rather than permitting disturbance.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.1101(k)(9) differentiates classes of asbestos operations and requires specific training methods and hands-on work for applicable classes. Core makes no abatement-class or hour-equivalence claim.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.1025(l) distinguishes general information from exposure-triggered initial/annual training, controls and medical programs. ESC06 awareness and hygiene do not replace the employer exposure-specific program.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.62(l) requires hazard communication, exposure-triggered training and annual training under its conditions, with actual job practices and medical protections. Core preserves that separate employer responsibility.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.1026(l) requires chromium hazard communication and demonstrated knowledge of the standard and medical surveillance. ESC06 teaches suspect coating assessment and exposure controls without claiming employer-specific training is satisfied.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.95(k) requires annual covered-worker instruction on noise, protection and audiometry; (o) excludes oil/gas well drilling and servicing from (c)-(n). ESC06 and the crosswalk explicitly retain this scope distinction.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.1030(g)(2)(vii)(N) retains interactive questions with the trainer; standalone orientation cannot claim to replace that role program.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.1020(g) requires initial and annual notice of record availability, custodian and access rights. ESC06 teaches requesting applicable exposure and medical records while keeping medical information private; employer notice remains required.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.1096(i) distinguishes NRC and state-regulated employers and requires applicable personnel instruction and accessible operating procedures. ESC06 preserves specialist authorization and does not grant radiation-worker or source-handling qualification.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.citation: General Duty Clause / state heat rules
rows.finding: OSHA heat guidance identifies workload, clothing and acclimatization as risk factors, prevention through cooling/rest/hydration, and immediate cooling plus emergency help for mental dysfunction. ESC06 teaches these decisions without inventing a universal heat threshold.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.141 covers sanitation, potable water, sanitary washing and separation of contaminated clothing; mobile crew facility provisions have conditions. ESC06 teaches designated clean facilities and contamination control; actual employer facilities remain required.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.178(l) requires formal and practical training plus workplace evaluation, qualified trainers and employer certification. Prior learning does not eliminate evaluation of actual equipment/workplace.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.602(d) expressly uses the operator training requirements of 1910.178(l). ESC07 distinguishes practical evaluation and employer authorization from this online orientation.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.601 applies to covered off-highway construction vehicles, requires safe brakes/restraints, backing controls and shift inspections with defects corrected. ESC07 teaches vehicle inspection, removal from service and coordinated backing without claiming road-license equivalence.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.201(a) incorporates MUTCD Part 6 for flaggers and warning garments. ESC07 teaches designated trained spotters and agreed signals; orientation does not grant traffic-control or crane-signal qualification.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.132(d),(f),(g) supports hazard-matched PPE, fit, demonstrated understanding/use and retraining. Respiratory and electrical protective equipment have separate provisions.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.133 requires protection matched to the eye/face hazard, side protection and suitable optical filters. ESC08 distinguishes impact, splash and optical hazards and requires task-specific selection; it does not certify every PPE selection.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.95 requires suitable, maintained PPE that properly fits each affected employee, with employer responsibility including employee-owned equipment. ESC08 teaches fit, suitability, inspection and employer hazard assessment.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.212 requires protection against points of operation, nip points, rotating parts and flying material; guards must not introduce hazards. ESC08 teaches these hazards and prohibits defeating guards or substituting a stop button for isolation.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.215 requires applicable guards and wheel mounting/inspection controls. ESC08 requires compatible ratings, sound accessories and authorized inspection, with a worked grinder rejection scenario; it does not qualify wheel installers.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.243 specifies guards and controls by portable-tool type. ESC08 teaches selecting appropriate guarded equipment and following manufacturer/task procedures rather than improvising switches or attachments.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.300 requires safe tools and guarding of hazardous moving parts and points of operation. ESC08 distinguishes construction provisions and teaches defect segregation and guarding without granting equipment-service authority.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.23 requires inspection each shift, removal of defective ladders, facing the ladder and a secure handhold. ESC08 teaches inspection, intended use, safe climbing and avoiding overreach/load interference.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.1060 requires competent-person instruction on applicable ladder/stairway hazards, placement, use, load capacities and needed retraining. General awareness alone does not prove actual equipment skill.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.38 requires role-specific alarm, evacuation and accountability procedures when a standard requires a plan; review applies at initial assignment and relevant changes.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.39(d) requires initial job fire-hazard information and review of the self-protection portions of the actual plan.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.37 requires unobstructed exit routes, working emergency safeguards and visible marking. ESC09 escape-route planning and ESC08 housekeeping retain actual site route verification.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.157(a),(b),(g) distinguishes evacuation policies, employee education and designated equipment-user training. No universal practical examination is inferred.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.151(b) addresses first aid when suitable medical facilities are not nearby; (c) addresses immediate corrosive flushing. It does not require every orientation learner to be a first aider.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.50 requires advance arrangements for prompt medical attention and qualified first-aid availability where medical care is not reasonably accessible. ESC09 keeps first aid within training and requires site emergency planning; the course is not a first-aid qualification.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.120(e)(3) distinguishes 40-hour and limited 24-hour roles and supervised field experience. Energy Core makes no HAZWOPER qualification or hour-credit claim.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1926.65(q) distinguishes emergency response roles and competencies with refresher and employer records; awareness withdrawal does not qualify a responder.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.106(e)(6) requires control of ignition sources including static, hot surfaces and sparks. The fire/hazardous-material instruction teaches ignition control and approved procedures without granting flammable-liquid system design authority.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.109 imposes specialized explosives handling and transportation safeguards, including qualified supervision for transfers. The core preserves exclusion and specialist authorization; it does not teach or authorize blasting.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.269(a)(2) requires task-specific training and demonstrated proficiency before training is considered complete. The core electrical lesson preserves qualified-person boundaries and does not substitute its quiz for electric-power qualifications.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: 1910.410 requires dive-task training, equipment and emergency skills, CPR/first aid and relevant hyperbaric knowledge. Core orientation is not commercial-diver qualification; specialized duties remain outside its credential.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: OSHA maritime standards identify distinct parts 1915, 1917 and 1918. The applicability crosswalk preserves maritime-specific work requirements instead of treating general energy orientation as maritime authorization.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: Part 1928 has its own agricultural scope and incorporated standards. Crosswalk retains agricultural task assessment; energy orientation does not qualify agricultural machine operation.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: OSHA State Plans must be at least as effective as federal OSHA and may impose distinct requirements. Crosswalk requires actual work-location review and does not represent federal mapping as all-state legal compliance.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

rows.finding: OSHA oil/gas standards guidance distinguishes other federal authorities, including radiation, hazardous-material transportation and explosives requirements. Crosswalk retains transport/offshore/mine/aviation/licensed-duty boundaries; no external license is conferred.
rows.result: orientation boundary consistent with cited clauses

note: 68 rows reviewed against cited sources for orientation scope; no blanket compliance or external qualification is claimed.
